name: Hacksaw Gaming
note: Lists every RTP version it licenses on each game page — usually four, e.g. 96.38% down to 88.42%.
licences: MGA, UKGC, Ontario, Greece, Romania, Denmark

name: Push Gaming
note: Game pages say RTPs may vary by casino and list both versions, e.g. 96.70% / 94.06%.
licences: MGA, UKGC

name: Nolimit City
note: Extreme-volatility studio in the Evolution group; each game page shows a single RTP.
licences: MGA

name: Relax Gaming
note: Money Train studio; its game pages don't publish an RTP.
licences: MGA, UKGC, Gibraltar, Ontario, Sweden, Denmark, Pennsylvania and more

name: Print Studios
note: Lists a base RTP and a separate bonus-buy RTP on each game page.
licences: Not shown on its site

name: Pragmatic Play
note: Volume studio; game pages show one RTP each without saying whether lower builds exist.
licences: Licensed or certified in over 30 jurisdictions (its claim)

name: Play’n GO
note: Publishes five RTP configurations for most titles — a 96, 94, 91, 87 and 84 band — in the game data on its own site, alongside which band ships by default and whether the title is approved in each jurisdiction it is licensed in.
licences: 24 jurisdictions listed, including Great Britain, Malta, Gibraltar, Sweden, Denmark, Ontario, Alberta, Québec, Michigan, New Jersey, Pennsylvania and West Virginia

name: Quickspin
note: States the versions outright in each game write-up: Cash Truck 3 Turbo "will arrive fully-loaded with 4 RTP versions, namely: 96%, 92%, 94% and 87%", and Epic Fish is "made available in 4 RTP versions: 96%, 94%, 92% and 85%".
licences: Malta and Great Britain

name: Yggdrasil
note: Footnotes the full set under the headline figure — Raptor 2 reads 97% with "RTP 97%,96%,94%,90.5%" below it — and its games index filters by RTP band, from 86% up to 97%.
licences: 8 jurisdictions: Malta, Great Britain, Gibraltar, Romania, Isle of Man, Greece, Belgium and Buenos Aires City

name: Blueprint Gaming
note: Goes further than any other studio here: it names the build as well as the figure. Eye of Horus is listed as BP_EyeofHorus90 at 90.25%, BP_EyeOfHorus92 at 92.04%, BP_EyeofHorus93 at 93%, BP_EyeofHorus94 at 94% and BP_EyeofHorus at 96.31% — so a build identifier in a lobby can be matched to a return.
licences: Great Britain, Malta, Gibraltar and Alderney

name: AvatarUX
note: Lists three configurations per title on the game page — Tempting Treats at 96.16%, 94.06% and 90.94% — and describes its games as shipping with "three configurable RTP profiles".
licences: Sweden, Romania and Malta

name: Thunderkick
note: Publishes a single return in the game-details block — Hot Potato Battleground reads "RTP 94.23" — alongside volatility and max exposure. Whether lower builds are licensed is not stated.
licences: Great Britain, Denmark and Ontario

name: Wazdan
note: One figure per game page, in a Game Info block — Mighty Wild: Gorilla reads "RTP: 96.2 %" with max win, volatility and release date beside it. No second configuration is mentioned.
licences: 6 jurisdictions: Malta, Great Britain, Romania, Greece, New Jersey and Ontario

name: Endorphina
note: A single return under Game Details — Lucky Stamps and Bazaar Monkey both read "RTP: 96.08%" — and the games index filters on a min/max RTP range, which only works because there is one figure per title.
licences: 9 jurisdictions: Malta, Romania, Denmark, Sweden, Ontario, Greece, Peru, Alberta and Anjouan

name: BGaming
note: Shows one return on each game card in its own catalogue, next to a volatility rating, and headlines the figure where it is unusual — Plinko is sold on 99% RTP. Lower builds are not listed.
licences: Malta

name: NetEnt
note: Keeps its own site at netent.com despite the Evolution acquisition, and each game page carries one return in a stats block beside release date, hit frequency and max payout — Divine Fortune at 96.59%, with a hit frequency of 20.00%. Whether lower builds are licensed is not stated.
licences: Malta

name: Red Tiger
note: Publishes on its own site at redtiger.com in the same stats block its sister studio NetEnt uses: Gonzo's Quest Megaways at 95.77%, hit frequency 26.25%, max payout 20,972x. One figure per title, with no second configuration named.
licences: Malta

name: Big Time Gaming
note: The studio that invented Megaways publishes a single figure under GAME STATS — Bonanza at 96.00%, across 117,649 ways. Lower builds of Megaways titles are common in the wild, and nothing on the page says which ones Big Time Gaming licenses.
licences: Sweden

name: ELK Studios
note: Its game pages are detailed — features, grid, max win, X-iter buy-in multiples — and carry no RTP at all. The game data goes into a downloadable product sheet instead of onto the page, so the figure is not where a player would look for it.
licences: Great Britain, Malta, Romania, Ontario and Greece

name: 3 Oaks Gaming
note: Game pages run to features, jackpot multiples and two dozen languages without stating a return anywhere. 3 Oaks describes itself as a distributor of content from other studios, which may be why — but it leaves the return unpublished either way.
licences: Great Britain, Isle of Man, Romania, Malta, Peru and Greece

name: Octoplay
note: Publishes everything except the figure that matters: its game pages carry hit rate, volatility, grid size and max win in a spec block, and no RTP.
licences: 13 jurisdictions: Malta, Romania, Greece, Great Britain, Sweden, Ontario, Denmark, Alberta, Michigan, Connecticut, Pennsylvania, Delaware and West Virginia

name: Microgaming / Games Global
note: There is no public game catalogue on gamesglobal.com at all — the site is corporate, and the only outward link from its footer is to its UK Gambling Commission register entry. Nothing about any individual title, let alone its return, is published there.
licences: 18 jurisdictions: Great Britain, Malta, Alderney, Gibraltar, Sweden, Denmark, Belgium, Greece, Romania, Spain, Ontario, Buenos Aires City, Peru, Connecticut, Michigan, New Jersey, Pennsylvania and West Virginia

name: Playtech
note: A B2B site organised by product line rather than by game. There is no public catalogue of individual slots on playtech.com, so no title's return is published on the studio's own pages.
licences: Great Britain and Malta

name: Evolution
note: The widest licence footprint of any supplier here — 32 jurisdictions, including five Canadian provinces and six US states. Its own brand pages carry no return for any title, which for a live-casino supplier is the norm: the house edge of a roulette or blackjack table follows from its rules rather than from a configuration a studio picks. Its slot studios keep their own sites, and publish there.
licences: 32 jurisdictions, including Great Britain, Malta, Sweden, Denmark, Ontario, Quebec, British Columbia, Alberta, Michigan, New Jersey, Pennsylvania and West Virginia
